strings.help.camera.enabled: Enable or completely disable this camera (disabled cameras do not connect to streams and do not take a grid slot).
strings.help.camera.main_source:
Main Stream (High Quality)
Always used for video recording, AI recognition, and detailed view. Accepts: rtsp://user:pass@ip:554/stream1, http://..., webcam index (0, 1), or local .mp4 file.
strings.help.camera.name: Friendly camera name (e.g., 'Gate Entrance', 'North Warehouse'). Used in the grid, window title, and search.
strings.help.camera.sub_source:
Compressed Sub-Stream (Low Resolution for Grid)
Displayed ONLY in the main grid tiles (e.g., rtsp://.../stream2 or channel=1&subtype=1) to avoid decoding 4K/FullHD for dozens of thumbnails. If left empty (e.g., webcam 0 or local file), the grid automatically scales frames from the main stream.
strings.help.camera.uuid: Unique camera identifier (UUID v4). Generated automatically on creation and binds the archive folder so you can rename the camera without losing history.
strings.help.general.archive_root:
Archive Root Folder
Disk directory (a spacious or fast drive is recommended for the video archive) where per-camera folders (<UUID>/<module>) and the shared faces database (faces_db/faces.txt) are stored.
strings.help.general.autostart_os_and_play:
Windows Autostart & Automatic Monitoring
Adds the application to the current Windows user's startup (HKCU\...\Run) and automatically starts polling all enabled cameras on launch.
strings.help.general.kiosk_mode:
Kiosk Mode (Lock Exit)
When enabled: blocks Alt+F4 / Esc / close button on the main window; exit is only possible with Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Q.
When disabled (default): all windows can be freely moved across monitors, resized, and closed normally.
strings.help.general.language:
Interface Language
Selects the application language loaded from JSON files in the lang/ folder (<code>.json).
Default on first launch is English (en). You can also switch language from the top bar in the main window.
strings.help.general.operation_mode:
System Operation Mode
• server (Server Mode) — all options, archive, video recording, saving plate/face/people snapshots, face DB updates, and auto-cleanup are enabled.
• operator (Operator Mode) — full live viewing and on-screen AI analysis (plates, recognizing already known faces, people/vehicles) WITHOUT any disk writes (recording, screenshots, auto-registering faces, cleanup, and window position auto-save are disabled).
strings.help.grid.active_border_color: Border color of the camera tile currently open in a detailed view window (e.g. #00ff88).
strings.help.grid.border_color: Default grid dividing line color (HEX, e.g. #00e5ff).
strings.help.grid.border_width: Single grid line thickness in pixels between cells and along outer grid edges (1–10 px).
strings.help.grid.cols: Number of columns in manual grid mode (1–8).
strings.help.grid.mode:
Camera Grid Mode
• auto — automatically calculates rows and columns for the active cameras and window aspect ratio (1x1, 2x1, 2x2, 3x2, 3x3, etc.).
• manual — fixed grid (Rows × Columns). If there are more cameras than slots, a ◀ / ▶ page switcher appears.
strings.help.grid.offline_border_color: Border color of a tile when connection to the camera stream is lost (e.g. #ff4444).
strings.help.grid.rows: Number of rows in manual grid mode (1–8).
strings.help.grid.show_fps: Show current sub-stream FPS on each tile in the grid.
strings.help.grid.show_labels: Show the camera name/description in the top-left corner of each grid tile.
strings.help.grid.show_status: Show status badges on each tile: ● REC (recording), active modules, and connection state.
strings.help.grid.tile_gap: Outer margin around the entire camera grid in pixels (0–20 px).
strings.help.hardware.ai_backend:
Neural Network Accelerator (ONNX Runtime)
• cpu — maximum compatibility on any PC (default).
• auto — automatically picks the fastest available accelerator (CUDA -> DirectML -> OpenVINO -> CPU).
• cuda — NVIDIA CUDA GPU (highest speed on GeForce/RTX cards; requires onnxruntime-gpu and CUDA/cuDNN).
• directml — DirectX 12 GPU (works on NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel without CUDA Toolkit; requires onnxruntime-directml).
• openvino — acceleration on Intel CPUs and integrated graphics.
strings.help.hardware.ai_max_fps_per_cam:
Max AI Analysis Rate per Camera (FPS, 1–30)
Limits how many times per second each camera sends frames to neural networks. 6–10 FPS per camera is enough for reliable plate and face recognition while saving 60–80% CPU/GPU resources with multiple cameras.
strings.help.hardware.ai_threads:
Threads per ONNX Session & AI Workers (1–8)
1–2 workers are usually enough for GPU. For CPU, increase cautiously while leaving cores for decoding, video encoding, and UI.
strings.help.hardware.display_detail_fps: Max refresh rate in the detailed view window of a selected camera (5–60 FPS).
strings.help.hardware.display_grid_fps: Max refresh rate for grid tiles (3–30 FPS). Using 10–15 FPS drastically lowers UI and CPU load with 8–16 cameras.
strings.help.hardware.use_opencv_opencl:
OpenCV OpenCL (Transparent API / UMat)
Enables GPU-accelerated frame resizing and image processing in OpenCV when an OpenCL driver is available and stable.
strings.help.hardware.video_decode_mode:
Input Stream Decoding Mode
• cpu — standard OpenCV VideoCapture (most reliable for webcams and local files).
• auto / d3d11va / cuda / qsv — FFmpeg GPU hardware decoding for RTSP/HTTP network streams (with automatic CPU fallback if unsupported).
strings.mod.faces.description: Biometric detection, frontality scoring, and face recognition with a shared person database (faces.txt).
Extend cooldown while the person stays in frame

Presence Mode (Sliding Cooldown)
When enabled: while the person remains in the camera's view, the cooldown keeps extending and NO duplicate photo is taken until they disappear for N seconds.
When disabled: a snapshot is saved once every N seconds while present.

strings.mod.video.field.codec.help:
Video Recording Processor & Codec
• copy — DIRECT RTSP/HTTP STREAM RECORDING without re-encoding! Almost 0% CPU and GPU load. Ignores CRF/FPS/Preset/Scale and splits on camera keyframes (not suitable for USB webcams like 0).
• h264_nvenc / hevc_nvenc / av1_nvenc — NVIDIA GPU hardware encoding (minimal CPU).
• h264_qsv / hevc_qsv — Intel QuickSync hardware encoding.
• h264_amf / hevc_amf — AMD Radeon hardware encoding.
• libx264 / libx265 — software CPU compression.
• mp4v — fallback OpenCV codec.
